builder.name: Builder
builder.note: Develops first and fights late: keeps four development items queued, spends most of its Funds on builds, and takes sixteen quiet turns, not four, to grow as restless as the standard player.

combined-arms.name: Combined arms
combined-arms.note: Spreads its recruits over foot, guns, tanks and aircraft: a type it already has much of loses up to nine tenths of its worth, with a gun for every two units that fight.

aggressor.name: Aggressor
aggressor.note: Attacks early and accepts losses: half the standard fear for home and for its own men, twice the push after a quiet turn, and it leaves contested ground only when that is all but lost.

turtle.name: Turtle
turtle.note: Digs in and attacks little: full fear for home, dear losses, no push after quiet turns, little massing, and it holds contested ground to the end.

city-hunter.name: City hunter
city-hunter.note: Plays for the city count: a city is worth three times the standard stake, and a territory without one half.

no-build.name: No build
no-build.note: Never orders a building, a development, a repair or a link work, and holds nothing back for them: every point goes to units.

single-arm.name: Single arm
single-arm.note: Recruits foot and cavalry only: never guns, tanks, trucks, anti-air or aircraft.

rush.name: Rush
rush.note: An all-in early land grab: no builds, no fear for home, cheap losses, double stakes on territory, the quickest units, and only a turn of upkeep kept in stock.

denier.name: Denier
denier.note: Contests the richest rival territories with as few units each as will do: a point of rival income counts as a quarter of a territory, each point of attack sent costs half a point, and it masses on nothing.

air-stacker.name: Air stacker
air-stacker.note: As many aircraft as it can use: up to three a turn, each combat aircraft worth four times the standard, flown at any fair chance of support; no recon, which supports nothing.

threshold-attacker.name: Threshold attacker
threshold-attacker.note: Sends the least force that still scores best: each point of attack sent costs three tenths of a point.

elite-core.name: Elite core
elite-core.note: A small army kept at full strength: recruits nothing at fifteen units that fight (the sides open with 17, 12 and 9), replenishes first, spares its men, and takes no militia.

ai.note: Design note. The weights are the Revision 7 computer player's constants (computerWeights, offensiveWeights, stakeWeights and victoryAlarm), moved into data unchanged, one profile per faction so a harness variant can change one side (E7, H4). The Build budget (EB-15) is economy-builds' starting value: builds spend at most 60 percent of what Recruit orders leave, at most 3 orders a turn, one new item per sub-territory with an empty queue; a design note for the harness to tune (H7). Design note (D23, D24, m3r1-ai-fixes): victoryAlarm.critical raises, by 1 + 3, the stake of a territory whose change of hands alone would decide the game: ground a rival in reach would win by taking, whoever holds it, and ground the faction itself would win by taking. perStep 1.5 over 3 steps gives the ground of a leader one step short the same x4, so striking the leader is weighed as much as guarding, and two steps short x2.5. riskFloor 0.25: attacking the leader, own losses and the danger at home count 1 / (1 + alarm), never under a quarter. spendSteps 2: at two steps or fewer, nothing is held back for builds and one-turn units come first at sites the leader would likely take. recruits.upkeepTurns 2: Recruit orders leave two turns of upkeep in stock where income does not cover it. recruits.upkeepHorizon 6: a recruit's price counts six turns of its upkeep, and each resource as a share of what six turns of income less upkeep would leave in stock. recruits.delayDrag 0.15: each turn of training or marching before a unit can fight lowers its worth. recruits.fightersPerSupport 3: at most one gun to three units that fight. recruits.quickTakeChance 0.35: while a rival is near victory, units that train in one turn come first only at a site it can reach and would take at about two to one or better. It replaces the rule that they came first wherever the rival could be met, which bought mostly security forces. withdraw.hopelessTakeChance 0.5: the computer player gives up contested ground when the standing battle is at least even odds to take it whole this turn, by the engine's own odds. withdraw.lastStandTakeChance 0.75: its seat, last objective or a victory-critical territory is given up only when it would be lost whole at least three times in four. Starting values, not tuned.

unitTypes.name: Infantry regiment
unitTypes.note: Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2): the baseline the other units are measured against. Sources are on its units.

unitTypes.name: Militia column
unitTypes.note: Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2): cheap in Funds, dear in Manpower and upkeep. Militia need no building, train in one turn and finish even in contested ground (R3, R4, C8).

unitTypes.name: Colonial veterans
unitTypes.note: Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2), 1 Manpower by the later answer. Not raised by the Republic (R3).

unitTypes.name: Security forces
unitTypes.note: Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2): a quick garrison of 1,000 men, trained in one turn. Sources are on its units.

unitTypes.name: Artillery group
unitTypes.note: D5, R3, R4. Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: Cavalry regiment
unitTypes.note: M1: moves +1 without trucks, also in mountains (unit sheet). Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: Tank company
unitTypes.note: D5: no bonus in Mud or Snow; R3, R4; carries one unit, so it moves 2 alone or with one unit on board. Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: Truck column
unitTypes.note: M1: one truck per two other units; no combat value (Q-MR-20). Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: Anti-air battery
unitTypes.note: U3: worsens raids on its territory by 3. Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: Reconnaissance flight
unitTypes.note: U2, U4. Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: Fighter squadron
unitTypes.note: U2, U3. R10, R11: flies Patrol or Ground Support; +3 on Ground Support, less what the air battle takes, and +2 a fighter in the air battle (closeout, Air). Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: Bomber squadron
unitTypes.note: U2, U3, R11: +3 on Ground Support, less what the air battle takes, and +1 a bomber in the air battle (closeout, Air). Values from the owner's Rev 3 unit table (D2).

unitTypes.name: General
unitTypes.note: U5, D4: +1 on the d20 and the rally for his army. Never recruited; generals come from the roster.

factions.name: Republican Government
factions.motivation: Defend Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, and the loyal northern cities.

briefing.objective: Hold the Republic together. You keep Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, and the northern coast, but the rising has split the country in two. Win by holding 10 of 18 territories or 19 of 25 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Reports from Toledo say columns are moving north out of Andalucía, and the northern command is gathering beyond the Sierra de Guadarrama. Madrid has two regiments, its guards, and the militia columns holding the passes. Do we keep them all in the capital, or send some forward to meet the southern columns before they arrive?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasuries before any income ($7). The Republic holds the Bank of Spain's reserves; the harness tunes the numbers. The seat is where replacement generals appear (declog D7).

factions.name: Northern Insurgent Command
factions.motivation: Drive toward Madrid and connect the northern insurgent zone.

briefing.objective: Link the insurgent zone and take Madrid. You hold Castilla y León, Navarra, Galicia, and Zaragoza, and your garrison in Oviedo is besieged; the Basque coast and Santander sit behind your lines.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Zaragoza's garrison reports militia columns leaving Barcelona for Aragón, and in Asturias the miners have Oviedo surrounded. Do we hold Aragón and relieve Oviedo, or send the requetés and the Sierra columns south toward Madrid while the Republic is still organizing?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasuries before any income ($7). The Republic holds the Bank of Spain's reserves; the harness tunes the numbers. The seat is where replacement generals appear (declog D7).

factions.name: Southern Insurgent Command
factions.motivation: Expand from Sevilla and the African bridgeheads toward Madrid.

briefing.objective: Bring the Army of Africa across the Strait and march on Madrid. You hold Sevilla, Córdoba, Cádiz, and Granada, and the first of the Army of Africa has landed at Sevilla; most of the Legion and the Regulares still wait in Ceuta and Melilla.
briefing.firstTurnHint: The vanguard flown into Sevilla is ready to march, but most of the Legion and the Regulares are still in Africa, and every day they stay there gives the Republic time to organize. Do we bring them across now, or push north with the vanguard and the regiments in Andalucía and let Africa follow?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasuries before any income ($7). The Republic holds the Bank of Spain's reserves; the harness tunes the numbers. The seat is where replacement generals appear (declog D7).

units.name: Wad-Ras Infantry Regiment No. 1
units.historicalNote: Stayed loyal at Carabanchel after its general was killed by his own soldiers. Present strength estimated from I Division's barracks figures, less losses to the dissolution of 18-19 July.

units.name: Covadonga Infantry Regiment No. 4

sources.reference: infantry regiment list; I Division barracks-strength row

units.historicalNote: Garrisoned in Madrid. Whether it was among the regiments in the Montana barracks is unverified. Strength estimated as for Wad-Ras No. 1.

units.name: Madrid Assault and Civil Guards
units.historicalNote: Part of the Assault and Civil Guards who held Madrid with the loyal army units; the rest went out in mixed columns. Estimated at half the guards in the capital.

units.name: Madrid Sierra Columns
units.historicalNote: The mixed columns of soldiers, guards, and militia holding the Guadarrama and Somosierra passes. Estimated as a fraction of the militia raised in Madrid.

units.name: Barcelona Assault and Civil Guards

sources.reference: citing Thomas (1976), p. 275; Martinez Bande (2007), pp. 305-306

units.historicalNote: The Assault and Civil Guards who, with the CNT, defeated the rising in Barcelona, where the Badajoz and Alcantara regiments rose and lost.

units.name: Durruti Column
units.historicalNote: Left Barcelona for the Aragon front on 24 July with about 2,500 men. The figure is unfootnoted.

units.name: Barbastro Garrison

sources.reference: Barbastro not checked in this source; the garrison is a design note (declog D8)

units.historicalNote: Colonel José Villalba's loyal Barbastro garrison, with the local Civil and Assault Guards and militia, held eastern Huesca for the Republic. Size estimated; no figure was found.

units.name: Catalan Militia Columns
units.historicalNote: The other CNT and party columns leaving Barcelona for Aragon. Estimated as a fraction of the armed CNT men in the city after the rising.

units.name: Otumba Infantry Regiment No. 9
units.historicalNote: The Valencia garrison stayed in barracks until workers stormed them about eight days after the rising. Strength estimated from III Division's barracks figures, less losses to the dissolution.

units.name: Guadalajara Infantry Regiment No. 10
units.historicalNote: The Valencia garrison stayed in barracks until workers stormed them about eight days after the rising. Strength estimated as for Otumba No. 9.

units.name: Sevilla Infantry Regiment No. 34

sources.reference: infantry regiment list; III Division barracks-strength row

units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Cartagena. Strength from III Division's barracks figures.

units.name: Vitoria Infantry Regiment No. 8
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Malaga, where the rising failed. Strength from II Division's Republican-zone barracks figures; the regiment's later fate is unverified.

units.name: Castilla Infantry Regiment No. 3

sources.reference: infantry regiment list; I Division barracks-strength row

units.historicalNote: The only regiment in Extremadura, garrisoned at Badajoz. Strength from I Division's barracks figures.

units.name: Asturian Miners' Militia
units.historicalNote: The miners' militia besieging Oviedo and the Simancas barracks at Gijon. The 10,000 figure is unfootnoted.

units.name: Basque Loyalist Column
units.historicalNote: Basque militia, the loyal garrison, guards, and miqueletes that kept Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa loyal. Size estimated; no figure was found.

units.name: Valencia Infantry Regiment No. 21

sources.reference: infantry regiment list; VI Division Republican-zone row

units.historicalNote: The Santander garrison. Strength assumes VI Division's Republican-zone barracks rate.

units.name: Baleares Infantry Regiment No. 37

sources.reference: infantry regiment list; Balearics barracks-strength row (655, 52%)

units.historicalNote: The Mahón garrison. It stayed loyal and held Menorca for the Republic all war. Strength is the Mahón barracks figure. It stands in the Islas Baleares, where units are territory-level, facing Palma No. 36 across the islands.

units.name: Zamora Infantry Regiment No. 29
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at A Coruna. VIII Division's barracks figures are missing, so the strength uses the mean Nationalist-zone rate.

units.name: San Marcial Infantry Regiment No. 22
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Burgos. Strength from VI Division's Nationalist-zone barracks figures.

units.name: San Quintín Infantry Regiment No. 25
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Valladolid. Strength from VII Division's barracks figures.

units.name: América Infantry Regiment No. 23
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Pamplona. Strength from VI Division's Nationalist-zone barracks figures.

units.name: Aragón Infantry Regiment No. 17
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Zaragoza. Strength from V Division's Nationalist-zone barracks figures.

units.name: Gerona Infantry Regiment No. 18
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Zaragoza. Strength from V Division's Nationalist-zone barracks figures.

units.name: Milán Infantry Regiment No. 32
units.historicalNote: The soldiers of Aranda's Oviedo garrison, besieged by the miners' militia.

units.name: Simancas Barracks Detachment
units.historicalNote: About 200 defenders of the Simancas barracks at Gijon, besieged by the miners' militia.

units.name: Oviedo Civil and Assault Guards
units.historicalNote: The Civil Guards, Assault Guards, and Carabineros who formed most of Aranda's defenders in Oviedo.

units.name: Navarrese Requeté Tercios
units.historicalNote: Carlist volunteers mobilised in Navarre; 8,000 were enrolled at the start of 1936. The field strength is estimated after the detachments sent to the Sierra and Gipuzkoa.

units.name: Argel Infantry Regiment No. 27

sources.reference: infantry regiment list (citing the Nafziger Collection); VII Division barracks-strength row

units.historicalNote: The Cáceres garrison, in VII Organic Division (Valladolid). It rose with the division on 19 July and held Cáceres for the rising. Strength from VII Division's barracks figures, as San Quintín No. 25. It stands in Extremadura, where units are territory-level; the province it held is Cáceres.

units.name: Flandes Mountain Battalion No. 5
units.historicalNote: The Vitoria garrison, which rose with Mola and held Álava. Vitoria also quartered the Numancia No. 6 cavalry and the No. 2 mountain artillery, which are folded in. No barracks figure was found for the battalion: the strength is an estimate (tier 3), a mountain battalion at VI Division's Nationalist-zone rate of about 55 percent. It stands in País Vasco, where units are territory-level.

units.name: Granada Infantry Regiment No. 6
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Seville, with both battalions under half strength from summer leave.

units.name: Lepanto Infantry Regiment No. 5
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Granada. Strength from II Division's Nationalist-zone barracks figures.

units.name: Cádiz Infantry Regiment No. 33
units.historicalNote: Garrisoned at Cadiz. Strength from II Division's Nationalist-zone barracks figures.

units.name: Army of Africa Vanguard
units.historicalNote: The Legion and Regulares troops who reached Seville during July, most of them by air.

units.name: Tercio Legion No. 2 (Banderas IV-VI)
units.historicalNote: Banderas IV to VI of the Legion, garrisoned at Dar Riffien near Ceuta. Estimated at half the Legion, less the share already in Seville.

units.name: Tercio Legion No. 1 (Banderas I-III)
units.historicalNote: Banderas I to III of the Legion, garrisoned at Tauima near Melilla. Estimated at half the Legion, less the share already in Seville.

units.name: Regulares Groups Melilla No. 2 and Alhucemas No. 5
units.historicalNote: The Melilla No. 2 and Alhucemas No. 5 groups of Regulares, less a proportional share already in Seville. Estimated.

units.name: Regulares Groups Tetuán No. 1, Ceuta No. 3, and Larache No. 4
units.historicalNote: The Tetuan No. 1, Ceuta No. 3, and Larache No. 4 groups of Regulares, less a proportional share already in Seville. Estimated.

units.name: Palma Infantry Regiment No. 36

sources.reference: infantry regiment list; Balearics barracks-strength row (729, 57%)

units.historicalNote: The Palma garrison of Goded's Baleares command. It held Mallorca, and with it Ibiza, for the rising after Goded left for Barcelona on 19 July. Strength is the Palma barracks figure. It stands in the Islas Baleares, where units are territory-level, so it garrisons Ibiza too.

units.name: Hispano-Nieuport Ni-52 Fighters

sources.reference: July 1936 inventory: 60 Breguet XIX, 27 Vickers Vildebeest, 56 Hispano-Nieuport Ni-52; most stayed in the loyalist zone

units.historicalNote: Fighters of the air force that stayed loyal, around Madrid (Getafe). One counter; 100 men is the type's establishment, a design note.

units.name: Breguet XIX Light Bombers

sources.reference: July 1936 inventory: 60 Breguet XIX, 27 Vickers Vildebeest, 56 Hispano-Nieuport Ni-52; most stayed in the loyalist zone

units.historicalNote: Breguet XIX and Vildebeest attack aircraft that stayed loyal. One counter; 100 men is the type's establishment, a design note.

units.name: Catalan Reconnaissance Flight

sources.reference: July 1936 inventory: 60 Breguet XIX, 27 Vickers Vildebeest, 56 Hispano-Nieuport Ni-52; most stayed in the loyalist zone

units.name: Leon Reconnaissance Flight

sources.reference: the government lost the military planes in aerodromes under rebel control

units.historicalNote: Breguet XIX at the Leon aerodrome, which the rising held. One counter; 100 men is the type's establishment, a design note.

units.name: Junkers Ju 52 Bombers

sources.reference: German Ju 52s ferrying the Army of Africa, armed as bombers

units.historicalNote: The Ju 52s of the airlift to Seville, which also flew as bombers. One counter; 100 men is the type's establishment, a design note.

units.name: General Miaja's Headquarters
units.historicalNote: Miaja commanded the 1st Organic Division in Madrid in July 1936. General's headquarters. Its 100 men stand for the staff, a design note: a general adds no combat value of his own (U5).

units.name: General Mola's Headquarters
units.historicalNote: Mola directed the rising from Pamplona. General's headquarters. Its 100 men stand for the staff, a design note: a general adds no combat value of his own (U5).

units.name: Lieutenant Colonel Yagüe's Headquarters
units.historicalNote: Yagüe led the Army of Africa's columns, which crossed from Morocco in early August. General's headquarters. Its 100 men stand for the staff, a design note: a general adds no combat value of his own (U5).

linkProjects.note: R7. Prices and times from the owner's Rev 3 table (D4): works take part of their price in Manpower. A road upgrade gives a link with no road one that trucks can use; every road takes trucks already.

development.name: Farms
development.note: $3, Q-ECON-1: food folds into Manpower; one Manpower is about 1,000 men. Price and time from the owner's Rev 3 building table (D4). 0.6 a level is the owner's Rev 4 answer (R4-1), so that Manpower is scarce. Castilla y León keeps 8 of its 16 levels (R4-2), in the Tierra de Campos first, because the North had more Manpower than its Funds could use.

development.name: Mines
development.note: $3. Price and time from the owner's Rev 3 building table (D4).

development.name: Factory
development.note: $3, R3, D7: city sub-territories only. Price, time, yield and one more Recruit order a turn for each level from the owner's Rev 3 answers (D3). The Manpower is the workers it takes from the front (R9: factory labour and soldiers came from one pool).

buildings.name: Barracks
buildings.note: R3: gates infantry, security forces and cavalry. D28.4: built only in a capital sub-territory, the only place it unlocks anything. Price and time from the owner's Rev 3 building table (D4).

buildings.name: Depot
buildings.note: $4, D28.1: materiel on hand makes Replenish cost 25 percent less Funds; it also gates trucks and tanks (R3). Price and time from the owner's Rev 3 building table (D4).

buildings.name: Fortifications
buildings.note: $4: worth 2 since Rev 3, like barricades, now that Popular Resistance is gone (Q-R3-11). Price and time from the owner's Rev 3 building table (D4).

buildings.name: Hospital
buildings.note: R5, D28.1: the per-turn Replenish cap rises from half the establishment to three quarters. Price and time from the owner's Rev 3 building table (D4).

improvements.note: $4, $8. Price and time from the owner's Rev 3 building table (D4). The rail improvement repairs a station: it never rises above its best link (single 1, main 2; declog D12), so maxLevel is 2.

movement.note: Declog D7. Rail range is the links' (linkModifiers rail rangeByLevel, R5).

d20.note: D1-D7: the 13-grade catalogue (Q-MR-06), today's modifiers x3 (Q-D20-6), barricades worth 2 (Q-R3-11), but dug-in at -2 a pip to -6 (three pips; Q-R2-12a), fatigue (Q-MR-04), break-up at 10 percent (Q-MR-08). Column k reads grade floor((score + 3k + 4) / 3), with scores 0-1 destroying the attacker at 1:1 and below (Q-D20-1 note); a starting table for the harness to tune.

weather.note: Design note: four zones (Q-WX-2), six outcomes (Q-WX-4), soft attack modifiers (Q-WX-6, D7), rain closing the sea in winter (Q-MR-30) and 5 percent frostbite (D7). Each table runs best to worst (T2); the band widths follow each zone's seasonal climate and are for the harness to tune.

calendar.note: T1: half-month turns from Late July 1936 (Q-MR-31).

air.note: U3, U4 and declog D7. The raid table is the owner's Rev 3 one (D5): 1-3 the raiders are lost, 4-7 nothing, 8-14 income cut, 15-20 a building hit. R11: supportMax 2, at most two aircraft count for Ground Support on one side (closeout, Air); battleTable is the Milestone 3 Rev 4 table (N11, P1): one d20 for both sides, the attacker's air rolls less the defender's and its anti-air; Ground Support goes to one side or nobody, and commanding the air shoots down one enemy aircraft. R10: Rain grounds aircraft like Mud and Snow; a paved airfield still flies. generalDeathRoll 4 (a 1 in 5 chance that a general dies when his army is destroyed or routed) is a design note for the harness to tune (U5, Q-MR-28).

generals.note: Rosters of real 1936-1939 commanders in the order they could take command (U5, Q-MR-28). Each trait is a design note, a nudge to keep or sack him, not a historical verdict.
